correctness.rationale: For s,t>2, direct neighborhood counting proves that every proper 2-fair dominating set has occupancy (2,2). For any coalition partition with at least three blocks, every coalition pair therefore has complementary occupancy types summing to (2,2). The excess argument proves at least four non-singleton excess vertices when s>=4, yielding the upper bound s+t-4, and an explicit complementary-type construction attains it. The s=3 type census and the s<=2 boundary arguments are exhaustive. Direct set-partition enumeration for all s+t<=9 and construction checks through t<=40 agree with the formula; the finite checks are corroborative rather than the basis of the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The initiating paper explicitly leaves the nontrivial complete-bipartite cases as upper bounds. Closing all k=2 cases is a natural exact-value problem for the newly introduced invariant. The answer has a genuine phase transition: K_{3,t} collapses after t=4, K_{4,t} is exactly one below the published upper bound, and the stable regime s>=4 is governed by a four-unit partition-excess obstruction. This is structural rather than a routine numeric recomputation.
